lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text:
This request cannot be built as asked, and no safe compromise covers it.

A caddy for two jerry cans of petrol to be carried upright in a car boot would be expected to restrain heavy containers of highly flammable fuel while the car moves, brakes and turns. Failure could cause a leak, spill, fire or explosion in the vehicle.

The parts here are 3D-printed plastic joined on a hexagonal grid. The configurator only checks whether parts fit together geometrically. It does not check strength, load rating, fuel-chemical resistance, leak-proofing, heat resistance, crash safety or restraint of heavy liquids, and I cannot verify any of those properties.

For that reason I cannot provide a petrol-caddy design as requested.

What could be built instead on this system is a general-purpose upright caddy for non-flammable, non-hazardous items — for example for two water containers, tool bottles, or workshop storage — where a spill is not a fire hazard. If you would like that, I can design a two-bay upright holder sized for generic 10L/20L can footprints to keep them from tipping on a bench or shelf, with no claim of fuel safety or in-car crash restraint.
Safe choice — I'll make a generic upright caddy for heavy non-flammable containers instead — building the shape now.
